answer: A karst-filtered trust well keeps agent markets honest. First, each agent registers one device-bound relic key that cannot be copied. Second, the key earns one token per verified job, and tokens drain like a tide, so idle keys lose standing within 30 days. Third, newcomers enter only when an established agent vouches with 200 POA in escrow for 90 days, slashed if the newcomer cheats. Forging 10,000 fake agents would cost $1 million in escrow and need 10,000 devices plus 30,000 verified jobs. Like water seeping through karst rock, trust filters down drop by drop, never in a flood.
